correctness.rationale: For area-uniform independent points, radius has density 2r/ell² and circular minimal angular difference is uniform on [0,alpha]; the intrinsic Euclidean-cone cosine law yields E d²=ell²(1-8 sin(alpha)/(9 alpha)). Strictly increasing/decreasing critical-point intervals follow from g-double-prime=8 alpha cos(alpha), g-prime(0)=-1, g-prime(pi/2)=4pi-9>0, g-prime(pi)=-17, g(pi/2)=16-9pi/2>0, g(pi)=-pi<0. There are exactly two critical points, and comparison f(pi/3)<f(pi) plus f(alpha)->infinity at zero establishes the unique global minimum and sharp equality. Monte Carlo and deterministic root calculations independently corroborated finite cases only.

value.rationale: The precise natural invariant is the mean of squared intrinsic pair distances for area-uniform points on an actual circular cone surface. With only lateral area fixed, it gives a dimensionless dispersion-design problem. The theorem supplies a sharp isoperimetric-style constant attained at a unique nondegenerate cone, proves that its nonmonotone fixed-area behavior contrasts with strict fixed-slant stochastic order, and exactly classifies a second stationary point. It is not a textbook coordinate renaming or an arbitrary parameter slice.
